title: Nuevo Laredo writer wins state novel prize at Tamaulipas Lee festival closing
excerpt: Luis Eduardo Torres Sánchez of Nuevo Laredo won the first Premio Estatal de Cuento y Novela Orlando Ortiz in the novel category for 'Pequeño jardín infinito,' with a 100,000-peso prize and publication of his work.
content:
A writer from Nuevo Laredo has won the first Premio Estatal de Cuento y Novela Orlando Ortiz in the novel category, taking home a 100,000-peso prize and publication of his work.

Luis Eduardo Torres Sánchez won for his novel “Pequeño jardín infinito.” José Carlos Orta López de Lara of Tampico won in the short story category for “Últimos ritos.”

The prizes were presented Sunday, Nov. 22, at the closing ceremony of the second Festival Tamaulipas Lee in Tampico, at the Barco venue. The two winners were chosen from 52 other submitted works.

The prize is organized by the Instituto Tamaulipeco para la Cultura y las Artes (ITCA). Its director, Héctor Romero-Lecanda, said the state government committed to creating the first literature prize named for Orlando Ortiz, and that with the governor's support the prize will keep recognizing Tamaulipas writers.

The prize carries the name of Orlando Ortiz to recognize the career of an author who championed other Tamaulipas writers for many years.

The festival ran for 12 days across seven municipalities, with more than 51 literary spaces and more than 40 authors from the state, Mexico and other countries sharing their work in Nuevo Laredo, Ciudad Victoria, Tampico, Madero, Reynosa, Matamoros and El Mante. The closing also featured the presentation of Ortiz's book “Prosa-ísmos.”

The festival was organized by the state government through the Secretaría de Bienestar Social and the ITCA, with support from the federal Profest program, as part of the Circuito Nacional de Festivales por la Paz.
